reasons: No tests are visible in this packet.
Colours are typed in directly, not from the shared colour file.
If the fragments request fails, the plant still draws with plain labels, which is handled.
Tool paths are typed in directly.

terms.meaning: A drawing area in the browser where code paints shapes and text.
A single character drawn as one dot in the plant.
The effect that makes nearer things look larger, giving a 3D feel.
One of the four stages (Code, Frame, Build, Intelligence) that the page moves through as it scrolls.
A browser setting that asks sites to tone down animation.
A React function, such as useState, that lets a component keep memory or run side effects.
A short real data point shown as text next to the plant.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the hero
sections.what: Brings in React tools for state and drawing, the router hook for page links, the data fetch tool, and the reduced motion check.
sections.why: These are the tools the component needs, and their roles are clear from their names.
sections.watch_out: The reduced motion check is read once when the component appears, so a change in device settings may not apply until the page reloads.

sections.name: BuildRegion, Fragments
sections.title: Regions and the shape of the facts data
sections.what: Names the six parts of the plant (scope, cost, schedule, evidence, lessons, signals) and describes the facts response: for each region a label, a count, a unit and a list of text snippets.
sections.why: Each region stands for a real data area, as the header comment describes.
sections.watch_out: The snippets come from the server, so their wording is not checked here.

sections.name: REGION_TOOL, REGIONS
sections.title: Tool links for each region
sections.what: Sends each region to a tool page: scope to Yard, cost and schedule both to Reality Scan, evidence to Yard sources, lessons to Lessons Learnt, and signals to Opportunity Map. Also fixes the region order.
sections.why: Lets a visitor click a part of the plant and go to the tool that holds its data.
sections.watch_out: Page paths are typed in directly, so a renamed page breaks its link without any error.

sections.name: STATES
sections.title: Stage names and dot characters
sections.what: Lists the four stage names shown at the bottom (Code, Frame, Build, Intelligence) and the set of characters used for the code-like dots.
sections.why: The names match the scroll story described in the header comment.
sections.watch_out: The scroll points that switch stages are set separately in the drawing loop, so changing these names alone does not change timing.

sections.name: REGION_RGB, hash, clamp01, ease
sections.title: Colours and small helpers
sections.what: Stores a colour for each region, and provides helpers: one gives a steady number for each index, one keeps a value between zero and one, and one gives a smooth slow-down curve.
sections.why: Steady numbers keep the plant's layout the same each time, and the smooth curve makes the build feel natural.
sections.watch_out: The colours are typed in directly rather than taken from the shared colour file used elsewhere, so a brand change must be made here too.

sections.name: Pt
sections.title: Shape of one plant dot
sections.what: Describes one dot: its 3D position, its region, its character, its build timing, and fields used while animating.
sections.why: Each dot carries its own timing so the build can be staged from the bottom up.

sections.name: buildPlant
sections.title: Building the plant
sections.what: Creates the fixed set of dots that form the plant: a gridded pad, storage tanks, process columns, a pipe rack, a half-built steel frame, a tower crane and a flare stack. Each dot is placed by rules, so the same plant appears each time.
sections.why: The header comment calls it a procedural process plant, so it is built by rule rather than stored as a picture.
sections.watch_out: Changing one number moves the whole layout, because the shapes depend on shared numbers and the stable number helper.

sections.name: CodeBuild (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up the drawing
sections.what: When the component appears, it sizes a drawing area, builds the dots (1,000 on small screens, 1,900 otherwise), marks roughly one in eighteen dots to carry a real fact, links nearby dots for the outline stage, and prepares glowing pathways and a character set.
sections.why: Fewer dots on small screens keeps phones responsive.
sections.watch_out: Finding nearby links compares many pairs of dots, so raising the dot count makes startup noticeably slower.

sections.name: CodeBuild (part 2)
sections.title: Sizing, tracking and placing each dot
sections.what: Keeps the drawing area sized to the window, tracks the mouse and scroll, and on every frame works out where each dot sits on screen. This includes the code-rain drop-in while it builds and a slight push away from the cursor.
sections.why: The header comment says the plant brightens and parts around the cursor, and builds from the ground up as the page scrolls.
sections.watch_out: Every dot's position is recalculated on every frame, which can strain slower devices.

sections.name: CodeBuild (part 3)
sections.title: Drawing the dots and real facts
sections.what: Draws faint link lines during the frame stage, then each dot as a character or a small square depending on build progress, then the real facts as short text beside marked dots. Facts are cut to 34 characters, and skipped on the left so the page copy stays readable.
sections.why: Keeps the page text readable while still showing real data on the plant.
sections.watch_out: Facts only appear beside dots on the right, or near a hovered region, so many facts can stay hidden.

sections.name: CodeBuild (part 4)
sections.title: Pathways, hover tags and click-through
sections.what: Moves glowing streams between dots, finds which region is under the mouse by checking every third dot, and shows a tag with the region's label, tool and count. Clicking the plant opens the tool for the hovered region. The four stage labels at the bottom highlight the current stage.
sections.why: Lets a visitor hover to learn what each part holds and click to open its tool.
sections.watch_out: Hover detection checks only every third dot, so a very small region can be missed. Clicks navigate only when a region is already hovered, so a click with no prior hover does nothing.

summary: The animated dark hero: a process plant drawn from code-like characters that builds itself as the page scrolls, with real project facts placed on it and links to the tools behind each part.
purpose: Gives visitors an animated picture of a capital project and a way to open the tool that holds each kind of data.
why: The comment says each part of the site is a tool, that hovering shows what a part holds, and that clicking opens the tool.
how: 1. Fetches the real fact snippets for each region. 2. Builds a fixed set of dots shaped like a plant, about 1,000 on small screens and 1,900 otherwise. 3. Marks some dots to carry a real fact. 4. On every animation frame, places each dot for the current scroll stage, the mouse position and the reduced motion setting, then draws it. 5. Shows a tag when a region is hovered, and opens that region's tool on click. 6. Highlights one of four stage labels as the page scrolls.
inputs: The fragments response from the API, screen size, scroll position, mouse position, and the reduced motion preference.
outputs: An animated canvas, hover tags showing label, tool and count, click navigation to a tool page, and stage labels.
risks: Drawing every dot on every frame is heavy, especially on slower devices. Tool links are typed in directly, so a moved page breaks its link. Clicks navigate only when a region is already hovered. Colours are typed in directly rather than taken from the shared colour file, so a brand change must be made here too.
debug: If the plant does not appear, check the browser console and the canvas size. If tags show no counts, check the fragments response from the API. If the page stutters, reduce the dot counts set in the setup section. If clicks do nothing, hover the plant first.
